taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "A low shrub with ascending branches, 2-6 dm. high".

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "2-6 dm. high".

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "A low shrub".

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "A low shrub with ascending branches".

traits.leaf_habit.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 408, Spiraea: key: "Leaves deciduous; carpels dehiscent on the ventral suture. 3. Spiraea".

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "Leaves oval or elliptical, rounded at both ends".

traits.leaf_apex.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "rounded at both ends".

traits.leaf_base_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "rounded at both ends".

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "crenate or serrate above the middle"; read as serrate, as most photos show sharp teeth.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: leaves "1.5-3 cm. long".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 8 mm to 18 mm wide, about half to two thirds as wide as long as in the photos.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "inflorescence flat-topped or rounded"; the genus key: "Panicle flat-topped"; drawn as a corymb.

traits.inflorescence_outline.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "inflorescence flat-topped or rounded".

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: inflorescence "2-4 cm. broad".

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: 30 to 100 small flowers to a cluster, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 71501350, 13742396, 136606818, 233507514, 382337049, 386273598, 386152994, 383833706): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 411, Spiraea densiflora: "petals rose-colored, 1.5 mm. long, obovate".

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: each flower 4 mm to 5 mm across its exserted stamens, about three times the 1.5 mm petals Abrams gives.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 411, Spiraea densiflora: "petals rose-colored"; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.stamen_exsertion.note: Stamens standing well out of the flowers, so the clusters look fuzzy, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 71501350, 13742396, 136606818, 233507514, 382337049, 386273598, 386152994, 383833706): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 411, Spiraea densiflora: "follicles oblanceolate".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 411, Spiraea densiflora: follicles "about 4 mm. long including the short beak".

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: follicles ripe in August and September, after the June to August flowers.

generator.params.note: Douglas spiraea's (spiraea-douglasii) values, changed by hand for subalpine spiraea: a low clump of many ascending stems (Abrams 1944 p. 410: "A low shrub with ascending branches, 2-6 dm. high"), small leaves and short internodes, and one flat-topped cluster 3.5 cm long at each shoot's tip. Not fitted to measurements.

appearance.organs.bloom.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 410, Spiraea densiflora: "inflorescence flat-topped or rounded, 2-4 cm. broad". Drawn as 10 short branches spreading widely, each forking again into small clusters of rose flowers.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low, twiggy clump of ascending stems with small oval leaves toothed toward the tip, topped by flat, fuzzy clusters of rose-pink flowers. Organ cards from hardhack's (spiraea-douglasii), recoloured and resized by hand.

allometry.note: 0.45 m tall at 8 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows in subalpine parkland. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from Abrams and FEIS, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from a built-in template.
